module: Third-party library lunajson: SAX-type (event-driven) JSON parser. You give it a table of callbacks; it calls them as it reads without building the full tree, which allows processing large files or streams split into chunks.
usage:
local sax = require('libs/lunajson/lunajson.sax')
local p = sax.newparser('{"a":[1,2]}', {
  startobject = function() print('{') end,
  key = function(k) print('key', k) end,
  number = function(n) print('num', n) end,
  endobject = function() print('}') end,
})
p.run()
notes: Callbacks recognized in `saxtbl` (all optional): startobject, key, endobject, startarray, endarray, string, number, boolean, null.
The object returned by newparser contains run() (starts parsing), tryc() (reads the next non-blank character), read(n) (reads n raw bytes, n >= 0) and tellpos() (absolute position in the stream).
`src` can be a string or a no-argument function that successively returns pieces of text (nil at the end).

newparser.desc: Creates a SAX parser on a JSON string or on a source function that supplies the text in pieces.

src.desc: JSON text, or function returning the next piece (nil when done).

saxtbl.desc: Callback table: startobject, key, endobject, startarray, endarray, string, number, boolean, null.

newfileparser.desc: Like newparser, but reads the file `fn` in 8192-byte blocks (the file is opened with io.open then closed at the end of reading).

fn.desc: Path of the JSON file (io.open, real disk path).
